questions.q: When is 'fix forward' generally the better response to a production incident than rolling back?
options: Whenever the bug is severe, regardless of how well it's understood
When the fix is genuinely small and well-understood, and reverting would reintroduce other problems already fixed since
Only when the on-call engineer prefers it stylistically
Fix forward should always be chosen over rolling back
questions.explain: Fix forward makes sense specifically when the fix is fast and well understood and rolling back would bring back other already-resolved issues.

questions.q: What does `kubectl rollout undo deployment/storefront-api` actually do?
options: It triggers a brand-new build of the application from source
It re-applies an earlier revision's pod spec, including its pinned image tag, without rebuilding anything
It deletes the deployment entirely
It pauses the deployment indefinitely
questions.explain: Because Kubernetes tracks deployment revision history, rollout undo restores a prior revision's exact configuration, including its image tag, with no rebuild required.

questions.q: Why does immutable, commit-SHA image tagging (from Chapter 4) matter specifically for rollback reliability?
options: It has no real connection to rollback
Each revision points at one specific, unchanging image, so there is always a concrete earlier version to revert to — unlike a mutable tag like latest
SHA tags make kubectl commands run faster
SHA tags are required by Kubernetes syntax regardless of rollback
questions.explain: If every deployment referenced a mutable tag like latest, there would be no distinct, addressable earlier version for a rollback to actually restore.

questions.q: What does Azure DevOps's per-environment deployment history let a team determine before deciding to roll back?
options: The exact dollar cost of each deployment
What was running before the current change, and exactly when the change happened
Which engineer is currently on vacation
The total number of lines of code in the repository
questions.explain: Deployment history answers the two questions a rollback decision depends on: the prior known-good state and the timing of the change that followed it.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what should happen immediately after a rollback completes?
options: Nothing further — the incident is considered closed
An investigation should begin into what actually caused the problem, since the rollback only stopped customer impact, not explained it
The rolled-back version should be immediately redeployed
All feature flags should be disabled permanently
questions.explain: A rollback restores service but doesn't explain the root cause — it's treated as the start of an incident review, not the end of one.
